editorial:
Three British teenage friends head to a sunny party holiday where drinking, clubbing, and hooking up are supposed to make the best summer ever. At first, the trip feels loud, fun, and full of possibility, but the story slowly turns serious as pressure to fit in makes consent feel blurry. You mainly follow Tara, who wants to seem grown up and keep up with her friends, yet is not ready for what happens after a night of heavy drinking. The movie keeps the focus on small moments, awkward jokes, and changing moods, so the fun slowly feels unsafe without becoming a lecture.

The standout part is the acting, especially Mia McKenna-Bruce, who makes Tara feel real and vulnerable. The pacing is patient, the dialogue sounds natural, and the tension comes from what people do not say. Pros include its honesty, emotional weight, and strong character work. Cons include uncomfortable scenes, a heavy mood, and little relief if you want a light teen comedy. Watch it if you like serious coming-of-age dramas.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Tara finally tells Em that she did not want to have sex with Paddy, and Em comforts her instead of judging her. The trip ends with the friends heading home, and Tara looks out the plane window with a mix of relief and sadness. The twist is that the movie never turns into a big courtroom or revenge story; the real ending is Tara naming what happened and beginning to heal.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves serious coming-of-age dramas and realistic teen stories.
